premise: In a kingdom that has finally resolved to be rid of them, a knight bound in body and honor to his king is sent to move the dragonkin along -- a nomadic people cursed never to hold a home, damned for an ancient broken oath. Their leader agrees to go, but only if the crown funds the tribe's long road to a new land; and because trust between the peoples runs thin, the knight stays behind as a living guarantor while his squire rides for the promised resources. In the weeks of waiting he comes to know the dragonkin not as the threat he was told of but as a people who can never stop moving -- and he falls in love with one of them. When the caravan returns at last, honest payment in full, it does not free him: it forces him to choose between the oath that defines him and the woman whose people can never settle. He can keep his home or follow hers. He cannot do both, and whichever he keeps, the other is lost for good.
hook: A knight sent to drive out a cursed, homeless people stays behind as the hostage that seals their departure -- and falls for the very people he is expelling. When the ransom he has awaited finally arrives, it does not set him free. It makes him choose which life to lose.
structureSketch: Part 1: the standoff and the wait -- captivity that becomes belonging; he comes to know the dragonkin and falls in love. Midpoint: the caravan returns with the honest payment. Part 2: the road and the choice -- ending in tragic sacrifice, one life kept and the other lost irrevocably.
